newsitem.title: GERMANY: Wiretaps in Iran's Berlin consulate - magazine.
newsitem.headline: Wiretaps in Iran's Berlin consulate - magazine.

text.p: A German news magazine said on Saturday hidden listening devices and a tiny transmitter had been discovered in the Iranian consulate in Berlin.
The report, released by Focus magazine ahead of publication on Monday, comes amid tension between the two countries over allegations that Iran ordered killings of Kurdish dissidents in Germany.
Germany's Federal Criminal Office (BKA) had been called in to investigate the case, Focus said. A spokesman for the BKA declined to comment on the report.

The magazine said Iran's ambassador, Seyed Hossein Mousavian, complained about the wiretapping to the German foreign ministry two weeks ago, brandishing several listening devices and saying a transmitter had been discovered hidden in a wooden beam.
Investigators had already concluded German intelligence had not planted the devices and were now investigating other possibilities, the report said.
The bugging allegations were being kept secret to prevent any further deterioration of diplomatic ties, Focus said.

Both countries have been trying over the past few days to defuse a row over German prosecutors' accusations that the Iranian leadership ordered the 1992 gangland-style shootings of three dissidents in Berlin's "Mykonos" restaurant.
Furious protesters have rallied outside the German embassy in Tehran several times, throwing eggs and tomatoes and calling for the death of the prosecutors.

Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani said on Friday he hoped Tehran could maintain good relations with Bonn, while German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel dismissed calls from some members of parliament to cut off diplomatic relations.
